title: Agreement with the bounded derived global sections
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, and $K\in D^+(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $C$ be a complex representing $K$ and let $a:C\to I$ and $b:C\to J=\operatorname{Kinj}(C)$ be K-injective resolutions [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. Put $\Gamma(T,M)=M(T)$, with its $\Lambda$-module structure and applied termwise to complexes [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then the unbounded derived global sections $\RGamma(T_{\Et},K)=\Gamma(T,I)$ of [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded] is canonically isomorphic in $D(\Lambda)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to $\Gamma(T,J)$. Here $\Gamma(T,J)$ is the bounded-below K-injective construction of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], carried out in $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$; for $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ it is exactly that definition. The comparison is the image under termwise global sections and localization of the unique homotopy class $u:I\to J$ with $u\circ a$ homotopic to $b$, and is natural in $K$.

proof.text: Choose a complex $C$ representing $K$ and resolutions $a:C\to I$, $b:C\to J$ using [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. They are quasi-isomorphisms with K-injective targets by [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. By [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded] the first construction is $\Gamma(T,I)$. The second is the termwise-section recipe of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] with the same coefficient category $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$, not a change to the underlying abelian-sheaf resolution.

proof.text: Write $Q$ for localization. Since $Qa$ and $Qb$ are invertible [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], form $\alpha=Qb\circ(Qa)^{-1}:QI\to QJ$. The bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], applied with target $J$, gives a unique homotopy class $u:I\to J$ mapping to $\alpha$; with target $I$ it gives a class $v:J\to I$ mapping to $\alpha^{-1}$. Injectivity with targets $I$ and $J$ gives $vu=1_I$ and $uv=1_J$ in the homotopy category. Injectivity with source $C$ and target $J$ also gives $ua=b$. Thus representatives $u,v$ are mutually inverse up to chain homotopy and the comparison respects the augmentations.

proof.text: Global sections on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is additive: sums and composites of sheaf morphisms are sums and composites on sections at $T$. A cochain homotopy $h$ between $f,g$ satisfies $f^n-g^n=d^{n-1}h^n+h^{n+1}d^n$. Evaluating at $T$ gives the identical equation for $\Gamma(f),\Gamma(g),\Gamma(h)$. Apply this to the two inverse homotopies from step 2. The maps $\Gamma(u)$ and $\Gamma(v)$ are homotopy inverses, hence are inverse in $D(\Lambda)$, since localization factors through the homotopy category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: For any other augmentation-compatible comparison $u'$, $Q(u'a)=Qb$ implies $Qu'=\alpha$. Injectivity of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] makes $u'$ homotopic to $u$, so step 3 gives the same isomorphism after global sections. For a morphism $f:K\to K'$ represented between derived objects $QC$ and $QC'$, lift $Qa'\,f\,(Qa)^{-1}$ uniquely to a homotopy class $I\to I'$ and $Qb'\,f\,(Qb)^{-1}$ uniquely to a class $J\to J'$, using the same bijection with K-injective targets. The two composites from $I$ to $J'$ both localize to $Qb'\,f\,(Qa)^{-1}$; injectivity with target $J'$ identifies them. Step 3 therefore makes the square commute after global sections. For $f=1_K$, the derived lift is $Qa\,(Qa)^{-1}=1_{QI}$, so injectivity identifies its homotopy class with $1_I$. For $f:K\to K'$ and $g:K'\to K''$, the composite of the lifts localizes to $(Qa''\,g\,(Qa')^{-1})(Qa'\,f\,(Qa)^{-1})=Qa''\,(gf)\,(Qa)^{-1}$; injectivity with target $I''$ identifies it with the lift of $gf$. For the $J$ resolutions the identity lift has image $Qb\,(Qb)^{-1}=1_{QJ}$, and the composite has image $(Qb\prime\prime\,g\,(Qb\prime)^{-1})(Qb\prime\,f\,(Qb)^{-1})=Qb\prime\prime\,(gf)\,(Qb)^{-1}$; injectivity with targets $J$ and $J\prime\prime$ gives the identity and composition equations. This proves canonicity, naturality and independence of choices, completing the claimed agreement.
